claim: ACME maps by parallel constraint satisfaction over structural, semantic and pragmatic constraints; with fixed parameters it settled the radiation/lightbulb and laser mappings within 220 cycles (typically under 100), with cycles barely depending on surface similarity.
agent_test: Mapping step: ask the agent to list candidate correspondences, score each on structure/semantic/pragmatic, enforce one-to-one; compare with free mapping at equal tokens.

claim: ACME is parameter-fragile on cross-mapped stories: with default inhibition it failed on cross-mapped unsystematic stories and needed retuning (inhibition -.2 to -.1) while children succeeded. Re-read of Table 15: systematic S/S 3, D 4, S/D 38 cycles; unsystematic S/S 3, D 4, S/D no success; retuning to inhibition -.1 or min -.3 restores success (gap search).
agent_test: Test cross-mapped items (similar objects, different roles); measure whether the agent maps by role or by surface object.

claim: Hummel and Holyoak (1997) argue that ACME and SME can map analogies of any size with equal ease and so are arguably overpowerful; on the unnatural boys-dogs mapping people tend to re-represent the analogs (6 of 8 students solved it in 3 min per Holyoak and Thagard; about 3 to 6 min with error feedback in Keane et al. 1994), though the evidence is only suggestive.
agent_test: Give an unnatural isomorphism task; check whether the agent re-represents rather than exhaustively matching, and its token cost.
audit_note: Hummel & Holyoak 1997 call current models 'arguably' overpowerful and say the evidence is 'only suggestive' that people tend to re-represent; 'only via re-representation' is too strong; the sources are one lab (Holyoak) and the 6/8 and Keane figures are cited second-hand in Hummel & Holyoak 1997 (the 6/8 is not found in the Holyoak & Thagard 1989 text).
claim_before_audit: ACME and SME-type global parallel mappers are over-powerful: they solve unnatural mappings (boys-dogs) that people solve only via re-representation (6/8 students in 3 min; about 3-6 min with feedback in Keane et al.).

claim: LISA's working memory is capped at about 4-6 role bindings in a phase set; the boys-dogs problem fails unless about 10 role-binding pairs are in the set, predicting capacity-linked failure on many-correspondence mappings.
agent_test: Increase the number of simultaneous correspondences in a mapping prompt; compare with chunked serial mapping at equal tokens.

claim: Access (retrieval) and mapping are dissociable: surface/object similarity helps retrieval more, consistent role assignment matters more for mapping (Ross 1989; Wharton 1994); LISA reproduced the signs of these effects but with exaggerated magnitudes (mapping 1.98 vs human .19).
agent_test: Separate analog retrieval from mapping in the scaffold; test retrieval by surface vs structure cues and mapping success separately.
note: Gap search: GPT-4 with a hint to use an earlier story had recall 1.00 but precision about 0.5 (surface-driven false positives); no spontaneous correct use without hint (Puranam 2025, single study).

claim: Human convergence-problem retrieval ordering (close analog > schema > far analog) was reproduced by LISA (Luce .43/.34/.23); far-analog retrieval is weak without a hint.
agent_test: Seed memory with near and far analogs; test whether the agent retrieves far-domain structural analogs without a hint.

claim: Pragmatic centrality shifts mapping: people (and LISA, by firing goal-relevant propositions first) map according to the processing goal (human 43% vs 35% economic goal; 29% vs 65% military goal).
agent_test: State the goal before mapping; test whether goal changes mapping vs goal-blind mapping.
audit_note: Numbers (43% vs 35%, 29% vs 65%) match Hummel & Holyoak 1997, quoting Spellman & Holyoak 1996, but both listed sources are the Holyoak lab and the human data come from a single experiment; Holyoak & Thagard 1997 is a same-lab review with no new numbers.

claim: In LISA an inference is made only if enough importance-weighted structure is mapped (at least 70%), so weak-constraint mappings yield fewer inferences, matching Lassaline (1996).
agent_test: Gate analogical inferences on mapping coverage; measure unsupported-inference rate with and without the gate.

claim: Copycat's core idea, building the representation while mapping (temperature falling, top-down pressure rising), is a design alternative to given-representation mappers; evidence is qualitative and it has been applied only to synthetic domains.
agent_test: Compare map-from-given-description vs interleaved re-describe-and-map prompts on re-representation tasks.
audit_note: The synthetic-domain-only remark is Musker et al.'s literature characterisation, not a systematic check.

claim: GPT-3 matched or beat UCLA undergraduates on text digit matrices (OR 1.88 generative, OR 6.27 multiple choice, N=40), letter strings (OR 1.76, N=57) and verbal analogies, but was below humans on story analogies (OR 0.37, N=54).
agent_test: Baseline analogy battery for the agent at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Webb's letter-string result does not generalise: counterfactual alphabets push GPT-3 below 0.1 on lookup-dependent tasks while humans stay stable; Lewis and Mitchell pooled accuracy humans .753 vs GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452 (table row labels ambiguous in PDF text).
agent_test: Run counterfactual-alphabet variants; do not trust base-form accuracy as evidence of abstraction.
audit_note: Table row labels are not ambiguous in the raw PDF text (Humans .753, GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452). Webb et al. later disputed the interpretation.

claim: Webb et al. reply: counterfactual failures are largely letter-index counting; GPT-4 with code execution matched humans (P=.496) on permuted alphabets while without code humans are better (P=8.9e-13). Whether this rescues 'emergent analogy' is disputed.
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool for index/counting steps and recheck counterfactual accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Adults and 7-9 year olds keep accuracy across Latin, Greek and symbol alphabets (adults .88/.91/.89, children .62/.66/.67) while four LLMs fall, most in the far domain (GPT-4o .85/.63/.48; Llama-405B .79/.74/.27; Gemma-2 .60/.39/.14). Numbers re-checked against the paper.
agent_test: Add a far-transfer variant of each task as a held-out check.

claim: LLM analogy success is partly shortcut-driven: GPT-4 story-analogy accuracy falls 86% to 72% when the correct target's sentence-level overlap is removed (humans 78% to 70%); strong answer-order bias exists.
agent_test: Shuffle answer order and paraphrase; require invariance before accepting an answer.
audit_note: Numbers match Lewis & Mitchell 2024 (GPT-4 .86 to .72 on 36 trials from 6 problems; humans .78 to .70; answer-order effect), but the only other source (Inani et al.) merely cites that work, so there is one source, and the paraphrase sample is small.

claim: On novel re-representation tasks (semantic words to symbol sequences) top LLMs match humans on default items but are brittle to permuted example-pair order and semantic-content changes; performance rises with MMLU.
agent_test: Test order-permuted exemplars; self-consistency across permutations.

claim: On ConceptARC humans score 83-97% per concept group versus GPT-4 3-33% (overall 91% vs 25% zero-shot, 33% one-shot, text-only).
agent_test: Run a ConceptARC subset with scaffold vs plain at equal tokens.
note: Dated: this is GPT-4 (2023). By 2025 o3 reaches 77.1% vs human 73% on text ConceptARC grids, but about 27% of correct outputs rest on unintended rules vs 7% for humans (d01).
audit_note: The 25% zero-shot figure is at temperature 0.5 (19% at temperature 0); per-group GPT-4 range 3-33% is zero-shot from the ConceptARC paper.

claim: Analogical prompting (self-generated exemplars) gives small average gains (about +4%; Codeforces GPT-4 Acc@1 16% to 17-19%) and only for large models; smaller models do not produce useful exemplars; 35 of 50 sampled exemplar sets were relevant and correct.
agent_test: Add a self-generated-analog step; compare to plain CoT at equal tokens, per model size.
note: Qin et al. 2025: on GSM8K/MATH with GPT-3.5, relevant self-generated examples (avg 52.4) were worse than no-example prompt (55.8) and than random ones (54.9 to 55.7); accuracy of the examples, not relevance, drove gains. Relevance did help on BBH (63.2 vs 61.9).

claim: Thought Propagation (propose analogous problems, solve, aggregate) beat IO/CoT/ToT on shortest path (TP .65 optimal vs ToT .22, IO .33) and creative writing; single paper, backends not fully confirmed.
agent_test: Replicate the analog-solve-aggregate loop at equal tokens against self-consistency.

claim: Key/value binding in external memory (ESBN, Webb, Sinha and Cohen 2021) let networks generalise learned rules to novel entities at 95% or better on all four tasks, with as few as 2 entities on same/different; relational-bottleneck models such as Abstractors (same group) show better sample efficiency on relational tasks; this resembles LISA-style role binding by analogy (the note's gloss).
agent_test: Not testable by scaffold; informs keeping relations separate from object attributes in prompts.
audit_note: The 95%-or-better with as few as 2 entities result is ESBN's alone (Webb, Sinha, Cohen 2021); Abstractors are reported as sample-efficiency gains, not that figure; all listed sources share authors (Webb, Cohen), so one research group.
claim_before_audit: Binding by key/value indirection or a relational bottleneck (ESBN, Abstractors) lets networks generalise rules to novel entities (95% or better with as few as 2 entities); a learned analogue of LISA role binding.

claim: Transformer attention is argued to implement pairwise similarity (as in ACME/LISA) and key/value indirection (variable binding); this is a theoretical argument, not an ablation.
agent_test: None direct; mechanistic probing would be needed.

claim: Human-LLM item-level profiles diverge: bigger LLMs score as high as humans (.85) on 18 Gentner stories but item difficulty correlates poorly with humans.
agent_test: Report item-level agreement, not just accuracy.
note: Item-level r = .526 only for GPT-4o-mini with the conventional prompt; embedding margin r = -.032 (d12).

claim: By 2025 reasoning models (o3, o4-mini) match or exceed humans on text ConceptARC grid accuracy (o3 77.1% vs humans 73%), but about 27% of their correct outputs use unintended or incorrect rules versus about 7% for humans; tools do not help text accuracy, more effort does.
agent_test: Score the stated rule, not only the answer; flag correct answers with spurious rules.

claim: Far, real-world-to-abstract analogy is still unsolved by frontier models: on ARCANA (200 tasks) the best model (GPT 5.2, pass@3) is 10.1 points below human pass@1 on strict scoring, and Claude Opus 4.5 is 51.6 points below.
agent_test: Use far-analogy items to test the mapping step.

claim: A Copycat-inspired LLM loop (propose, slip, introspect, execute, reflect) solved 9/17 hard ARCANA tasks in about 2.2 loops, but there is no control arm and the authors call it non-general; interleaved re-representation has not been shown better than a fixed description.
agent_test: Run a matched test: fixed description vs re-describe-on-error at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieval of an analog and its correct application are separate steps in GPT-4: with a hint the model uses the correct source every time (recall 1.00) but also uses a wrong one about half the time (precision 0.50-0.52); humans are the reverse (precision 0.67-0.75, recall 0.26-0.39).
agent_test: Add a structure-based match check before transfer; do not accept retrieval by surface similarity.

claim: Reasoning models do not stay robust on analogy as task size and perceptual uncertainty grow: o3-mini falls 86.6% to 17.0% and R1 80.6% to 23.2% on I-RAVEN-X, o3-mini despite about 3.4x more reasoning tokens (and only 31.0% at high effort); separately, non-reasoning Llama-3.1 70B letter-string accuracy falls 0.35 to 0.00 as the alphabet is permuted.
agent_test: Cap binding count per step; move the heavy rule application to code or a checker.
audit_note: All numbers match, but I-RAVEN-X raises rule length, value range and perceptual noise (not 'binding load'), the 3.4x token figure is o3-mini only (5445 to 18482), and the Llama-3.1 70B letter-string result is a non-reasoning model that says nothing about long chain of thought.
claim_before_audit: Long chain of thought does not rescue analogy under growing binding load: o3-mini falls 86.6% to 17.0% and R1 80.6% to 23.2% on I-RAVEN-X with 3.4x more reasoning tokens; Llama-3.1 70B letter-string accuracy falls 0.35 to 0.00 as the alphabet is permuted.

claim: Small transformers learn letter-string analogies and reach 93.9% on new alphabets only when copy tasks induce matching heads between example input and output; they still fail on new transformations (12.3% to 13.1%).
agent_test: Supports an explicit input-output matching step in the prompt.

claim: In open 7B-14B models, relational information is held in mid-upper layers and failures are split between missing relation and failure to apply it; patching fixed up to 38% of failures. Abstract previous/next concepts have no invariant vector.
agent_test: State the relation in words, then apply it to the target in a separate step.
